I still remember the first time in my life that I got the Microshaft. The year was 1998, and a "fast" processor ran at a blazing 350 MHz. There was a problem with Windows 95 though, which would cause it to fail to boot if the CPU was faster than 300 MHz or so. Microshaft published a patch for this, but in an attempt to waste the time and empty the wallet of the consumer, the patch needed to be installed from a running Windows environment.

That's right, if you tried to run the patch .exe from DOS, it would tell you that it must be run from Windows, when the fucking problem was that Windows would not start, not even in the limited modes. So, what did this patch actually do? It was a self-extracting archive that would update some core Windows files with new versions; no technical reason it couldn't work from DOS. So, what did I do? I extracted the files from the patch on a different Windows machine, and then I manually copied them over on the affected one. Something that should have taken 10 seconds ended up taking 10 minutes.

I've disliked this company ever since.

Daily Devotional

July 26

18 While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal. (2 Corinthians 4:18 KJV)

Paul is telling us how he stayed positive in this world. He kept his mind on the spiritual things (things not seen), instead of physical things. If all we think on are the physical things of this world, we will be most miserable (1 Corinthians 15:19). This does not mean we are to ignore the physical things in life, as we must live in this world, but if we will keep our focus on the invisible things (spiritual things) then we will have the hope and promise, the Word of God promises us. We must remember that the physical things in this world are only temporary, and will all pass away some day (Mark 13:31, 2 Peter 3:10), but the spiritual (unseen) things are eternal and will never pass away.

What we think on, as well as what we speak (Proverbs 18:21), is so very important to our living a happy and fulfilled life. If we only think on carnal things it will bring death, but if we think on spiritual things it will bring life and peace (Romans 8:6). The Christian must keep his mind on spiritual things to be able to live the victorious life that God intends for us to live. Thank you Lord, for giving us Your Word.
